question: 0.25 g of an organic compound, on treatment with fuming nitric acid followed by AgNO3, gave 0.22 g of AgBr. The percentage of bromine in the compound is ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 37.45%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• This is a problem of Carius method for estimating halogen (bromine) in an organic compound.

◦ Formula: % of Br = (Atomic mass of Br / Molar mass of AgBr) × (mass of AgBr / mass of compound) × 100.

◦ Atomic mass of Br = 80; Molar mass of AgBr = 108 + 80 = 188.

◦ % of Br = (80 / 188) × (0.22 / 0.25) × 100 ≈ 37.45%.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• In the Carius method, the organic compound is heated with fuming nitric acid and silver nitrate (AgNO₃) in a sealed Carius tube; the halogen forms a silver halide (AgCl, AgBr, AgI) precipitate that is weighed.

NOTE

• Silver halide molar masses: AgCl = 143.5, AgBr = 188, AgI = 235. This method is used for the quantitative estimation of halogens in organic compounds.

question: Rani ki Vav is a UNESCO world heritage monument, situated in which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Rani ki Vav" (the Queen's Stepwell) is a UNESCO World Heritage Site located at Patan in Gujarat, on the banks of the Saraswati River. (रानी की वाव — गुजरात)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• It was built in the 11th century by Queen Udayamati in memory of her husband King Bhimdev I of the Solanki (Chaulukya) dynasty.

• It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2014 and features on the ₹100 currency note.

NOTE

• Other UNESCO World Heritage Sites in Gujarat: Champaner-Pavagadh Archaeological Park, the Historic City of Ahmedabad, and Dholavira (a Harappan site).

question: Bathukamma festival is celebrated in which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Telangana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Bathukamma" is a colourful floral festival celebrated predominantly by the women of Telangana (and some parts of Andhra Pradesh). (बतुकम्मा — तेलंगाना)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• It is celebrated during the Navaratri period (September–October) and honours the goddess Gauri (Maha Gauri).

• Women arrange seasonal flowers in concentric layers to form a "Bathukamma" and sing and dance around it.

NOTE

• Other festivals of Telangana include Bonalu (dedicated to Goddess Mahakali). Bathukamma marks the beauty of nature and the onset of the festive season.

question: What is the collection of Vedic hymns or 'mantras' called?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Samhita.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Samhita" is the collection of Vedic hymns or 'mantras'. Each Veda has its Samhita — the core collection of hymns. (संहिता — वैदिक मंत्रों का संग्रह)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Each Veda is traditionally divided into four parts: Samhita (hymns), Brahmana (rituals/explanations), Aranyaka (forest treatises) and Upanishad (philosophy).

• The four Vedas are Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda and Atharvaveda. The Rigveda is the oldest.

NOTE

• Shruti ("that which is heard") includes the Vedas; Smriti ("that which is remembered") includes texts like the Manusmriti, Puranas and epics.

question: Usha Barle, who won Padma Shri 2023, is popularly associated with which genre of music?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pandwani.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Usha Barle, a Padma Shri 2023 awardee, is a renowned exponent of "Pandwani", a traditional folk singing/storytelling art form of Chhattisgarh based on the Mahabharata. (पंडवानी — उषा बारले)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Pandwani narrates tales of the Pandavas; the singer performs with a tambura and expressive gestures. Teejan Bai is its most famous exponent.

• The Padma Shri is the fourth-highest civilian award of India.

NOTE

• Lavani is a folk form of Maharashtra; Panihari and Kajari are folk songs associated with Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh/Bihar respectively.

question: In which of the following years India hosted the Women's Asia Cup ODI Cricket?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2006.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India hosted the Women's Asia Cup ODI Cricket in the year 2006. (महिला एशिया कप — 2006)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Indian women's cricket team has been the most dominant side in the Women's Asia Cup, winning the title multiple times.

• The Asia Cup is organised by the Asian Cricket Council (ACC).

NOTE

• India's women's cricket has produced stars like Mithali Raj, Jhulan Goswami, Harmanpreet Kaur and Smriti Mandhana.

question: Alarmel Valli was associated with which of the following dances?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatanatyam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Alarmel Valli is a celebrated exponent of the Bharatanatyam classical dance form, known for the Pandanallur style. (भरतनाट्यम — अलार्मेल वल्ली)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Bharatanatyam is the classical dance of Tamil Nadu, based on the Natya Shastra of Bharat Muni.

• Alarmel Valli has been honoured with the Padma Bhushan and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

NOTE

• The eight classical dances of India: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (North India), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

question: When protein-rich gelatinous egg white is heated, it turns to solid white due to:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Protein Denaturation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When egg white is heated, its proteins (mainly albumin) unfold and change structure permanently — this is called "protein denaturation" — turning the clear gelatinous liquid into a solid white. (प्रोटीन विकृतीकरण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Denaturation is the loss of the natural (native) three-dimensional structure of a protein due to heat, acids, or other agents, though the peptide bonds are not broken.

• The change is usually irreversible (a boiled egg cannot become raw again).

NOTE

• Emulsification = mixing of two immiscible liquids (oil and water); Fermentation = breakdown by microbes; Gluten formation occurs in wheat dough — none of these explain the setting of egg white.

question: In which of the following states are the Nor Westers known as 'Bardoisila'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Assam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In Assam, the violent pre-monsoon thunderstorms known as Nor'westers (Kalbaisakhi) are locally called "Bardoisila". (असम — बरदोईछिला)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• In West Bengal, the same Nor'westers are called "Kalbaisakhi" (the calamity of the month of Baisakh).

• These storms bring heavy rain and strong winds and are beneficial for tea, jute and rice cultivation.

NOTE

• Pre-monsoon showers have local names: "Mango showers" (Kerala/Karnataka), "Blossom showers" (Karnataka coffee), "Kalbaisakhi" (West Bengal), "Bardoisila" (Assam).

question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct?
A) Balshastri Jambhekar started the first Anglo-Maratha newspaper - 'Durpun', in 1832.
B) He is remembered as the father of Marathi journalism.
C) Balshastri Jambhekar published the first Marathi monthly magazine - 'Digdurshun' in 1840.
solution_text:
The correct answer is A, B and C.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• All three statements about Balshastri Jambhekar are correct:

◦ A) He started the first Anglo-Marathi newspaper "Durpun (Darpan)" in 1832.

◦ B) He is remembered as the "Father of Marathi Journalism".

◦ C) He published the first Marathi monthly magazine "Digdurshun (Digdarshan)" in 1840.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Balshastri Jambhekar (1812–1846) was a social reformer, journalist and educationist from Maharashtra.

• "Darpan" was a bilingual paper (Marathi and English) that promoted social reform and modern education.

NOTE

• The father of Indian journalism is often considered James Augustus Hicky, who started the "Bengal Gazette" (Hicky's Gazette) in 1780, India's first newspaper.

question: Identify the correct statement with reference to the Padma awards.
option_1: The Padma award can be used as a suffix or prefix to the awardees' name
option_2: The total number of Padma awards to be given in a year should not more than 150.
option_3: The Padma Awards are given annually.
option_4: The names of the awardees are never published in the Gazette of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Padma Awards are given annually.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Padma Awards are announced every year on Republic Day (26 January) — i.e., they are given annually. This is the correct statement. (पद्म पुरस्कार — प्रतिवर्ष)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Padma Awards are of three categories: Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan and Padma Shri (in decreasing order of importance).

• The awards should not be used as a prefix or suffix to the awardee's name (so option 1 is wrong).

• The total number given in a year is generally not more than 120 (excluding posthumous, NRI/foreigner cases), so option 2 (150) is wrong.

NOTE

• The Bharat Ratna is India's highest civilian award, followed by Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan and Padma Shri. Padma awards are conferred by the President of India.

question: Which of the following is NOT a component of revenue receipt?
option_3: Fees paid for the registration of property
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amount borrowed from World Bank.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Amount borrowed from the World Bank" is a capital receipt, NOT a revenue receipt, because borrowing creates a liability (it has to be repaid). (उधार ली गई राशि — पूँजीगत प्राप्ति)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Revenue receipts neither create a liability nor reduce assets — e.g., taxes (GST), fees, fines, grants. So GST, registration fees and grants from UNESCO are revenue receipts.

• Capital receipts either create a liability (borrowings) or reduce assets (disinvestment).

NOTE

• Government receipts = Revenue Receipts (tax + non-tax) + Capital Receipts (borrowings, recovery of loans, disinvestment). Borrowings always fall under capital receipts.

question: According to the Census of India 2011, what was the population growth rate in Kerala?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 4.9%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Census of India 2011, Kerala recorded a decadal (2001–2011) population growth rate of about 4.9% — the lowest among all the major states of India. (केरल — 4.9%)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Kerala's low growth rate is attributed to its high literacy, better healthcare, women's empowerment and effective family planning.

• India's overall decadal growth rate (2001–2011) was 17.7%.

NOTE

• Kerala also has the highest literacy rate and a favourable (high) sex ratio in India. The Census of India 2011 was the 15th National Census and was conducted under C. Chandramauli.

question: In April 2023, who was appointed as the chairman of the National Technical Research Organisation (NTRO) by the centre?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arun Sinha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In April 2023, Arun Sinha was appointed as the Chairman of the National Technical Research Organisation (NTRO) by the central government. (अरुण सिन्हा — NTRO अध्यक्ष)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The NTRO is a technical intelligence agency under the National Security Adviser (NSA) in the Prime Minister's Office (PMO).

• It was established in 2004 and works in areas such as satellite and terrestrial monitoring, cyber security and cryptology.

NOTE

• India's key intelligence agencies: RAW (external intelligence), IB (Intelligence Bureau) (internal), and NTRO (technical intelligence). The current NSA is Ajit Doval.

question: Which of the following is an example of the first garden-tomb on the Indian subcontinent?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Humayun's tomb.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Humayun's Tomb" in Delhi is the first garden-tomb (charbagh-style tomb) on the Indian subcontinent. (हुमायूँ का मकबरा — पहला उद्यान-मकबरा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• It was built in 1570 by Bega Begum (Haji Begum), the widow of Emperor Humayun, and designed by the Persian architect Mirak Mirza Ghiyas.

• It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1993 and is said to have inspired the design of the Taj Mahal.

NOTE

• The "charbagh" is a four-part Persian-style garden divided by walkways or water channels. Humayun's Tomb was the first major Mughal building to use red sandstone on such a large scale.

question: According to the Census 2011, what was the annual population growth rate of India (in percentage)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1.64%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Census 2011, the annual (average) population growth rate of India was about 1.64%. (भारत की वार्षिक जनसंख्या वृद्धि दर — 1.64%)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The decadal (10-year) growth rate for 2001–2011 was 17.7%, which corresponds to an average annual growth of roughly 1.64%.

• The Census 2011 recorded India's total population at about 121 crore (1.21 billion).

NOTE

• The Census of India is conducted every ten years; the first synchronous census was in 1881. The 2011 Census had the theme "Our Census, Our Future".

question: The Indian Forest Service was created under the All India Service Act, 1951 in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1966.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Indian Forest Service (IFS) was constituted in 1966 under the All India Services Act, 1951. It is one of the three All India Services. (भारतीय वन सेवा — 1966)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The three All India Services are the IAS (Indian Administrative Service), IPS (Indian Police Service) and IFoS (Indian Forest Service).

• The IFS manages the country's forests, wildlife and environment; officers are trained at the Indira Gandhi National Forest Academy, Dehradun.

NOTE

• The IAS and IPS have their roots in the pre-independence Imperial services, while the IFS was created after independence in 1966. All India Services are governed by Article 312 of the Constitution.

question: Organisation of agriculture and animal husbandry is included in which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 48.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 48 of the Constitution deals with the "Organisation of agriculture and animal husbandry" on modern and scientific lines, and the preservation and improvement of breeds and prohibition of slaughter of cows and other cattle. (अनुच्छेद 48)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Article 48 is a Directive Principle of State Policy (DPSP) under Part IV of the Constitution.

• Article 48A (added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976) deals with the protection of the environment, forests and wildlife.

NOTE

• Other DPSPs: Article 45 (early childhood care/education), Article 46 (promotion of SCs/STs and weaker sections), Article 47 (raising the level of nutrition and public health).

question: In which of the following Indian states is the M.A. Chidambaram Stadium located?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "M.A. Chidambaram Stadium" (also known as Chepauk Stadium) is a famous cricket stadium located in Chennai, Tamil Nadu. (एम.ए. चिदंबरम स्टेडियम — तमिलनाडु)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• It is one of the oldest cricket stadiums in India and is the home ground of the Tamil Nadu cricket team and the IPL franchise Chennai Super Kings (CSK).

• It is managed by the Tamil Nadu Cricket Association (TNCA).

NOTE

• Other major cricket stadiums: Eden Gardens (Kolkata), Wankhede Stadium (Mumbai), M. Chinnaswamy Stadium (Bengaluru) and the Narendra Modi Stadium (Ahmedabad — the world's largest).

question: The famous English novel 'Em and the Big Hoom' is written by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jerry Pinto.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The famous English novel "Em and the Big Hoom" was written by Jerry Pinto. (जेरी पिंटो)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The novel, published in 2012, deals with a family coping with a mother's mental illness (bipolar disorder) and won the Hindu Literary Prize and the Windham–Campbell Prize.

• Jerry Pinto is an Indian writer, poet and journalist based in Mumbai.

NOTE

• Notable books: Amitav Ghosh ("The Shadow Lines", "The Hungry Tide"), Shashi Tharoor ("The Great Indian Novel", "Why I Am a Hindu"), Esther David ("The Book of Rachel").

question: Which of the following is NOT an element of weather?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Plants.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Plants" are NOT an element of weather. The main elements of weather are temperature, humidity, air pressure, wind, and rainfall/precipitation. (पौधे — मौसम का तत्व नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Weather is the day-to-day state of the atmosphere at a place, while climate is the average weather over a long period (about 30 years).

• Weather is studied under meteorology.

NOTE

• Elements/components of weather and climate: temperature, atmospheric pressure, wind, humidity, cloudiness and precipitation. Plants are part of the biosphere, not the atmosphere.

question: Which of the following organisms is used in bread and alcohol industries?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Yeast.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Yeast" (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) is a fungus used in the bread and alcohol (brewing) industries. It carries out fermentation, converting sugars into carbon dioxide and alcohol. (यीस्ट / खमीर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• In bread-making, the CO₂ released by yeast makes the dough rise (leavening).

• In the alcohol industry, yeast ferments sugars to produce ethanol (as in beer and wine).

NOTE

• Clostridium and Nitrobacter are bacteria (Nitrobacter helps in nitrogen fixation/nitrification); Penicillium is a fungus used to make the antibiotic penicillin.

question: In Union Budget 2023-24, annual production of 5 MMT under Green Hydrogen Mission is to be targeted by the year ___________ to facilitate transition of the economy to low carbon intensity.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2030.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Union Budget 2023-24, under the National Green Hydrogen Mission, an annual production of 5 MMT (Million Metric Tonnes) of green hydrogen is targeted by the year 2030, to facilitate the economy's transition to low carbon intensity. (हरित हाइड्रोजन मिशन — 2030)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The National Green Hydrogen Mission was approved in January 2023 with an outlay of about ₹19,700 crore.

• Green hydrogen is produced by the electrolysis of water using renewable energy, producing no carbon emissions.

NOTE

• India aims to become a global hub for green hydrogen production and export, supporting its goal of achieving net-zero carbon emissions by 2070.

question: The Prime Minister in India is ________.
option_3: the Supreme Commander of Armed Forces
solution_text:
The correct answer is the real executive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In India, the Prime Minister is the real executive (de facto head) who actually exercises executive power and runs the government. (प्रधानमंत्री — वास्तविक कार्यपालिका)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The President is the nominal/constitutional head (de jure) and also the Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces.

• The Prime Minister is the head of the Council of Ministers and the leader of the majority party in the Lok Sabha.

NOTE

• Article 74 provides that the President acts on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister. The Chief Justice of India heads the judiciary, not the PM.

question: According to the Census of India-2011, what is the share of workforce engaged in the agriculture sector?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 54.6%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Census of India 2011, about 54.6% of the total workforce was engaged in the agriculture sector (as cultivators and agricultural labourers). (कृषि क्षेत्र में कार्यबल — 54.6%)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• This shows that a majority of Indians still depend on agriculture and allied activities for their livelihood, even though its share in GDP is much smaller (around 15–18%).

• The workforce is classified as main workers, marginal workers and non-workers in the Census.

NOTE

• Agriculture is the primary sector of the economy. India's large agricultural workforce reflects disguised unemployment in rural areas.
